Create 13 realistic, hand-written-looking text documents for testing a YAML/Markdown/Python/R formatter. Write them into the directory /tmp/corpus7/j/ (create it). Do NOT run any formatter or other program on them; just write the files with the Write tool (or a shell heredoc). Do not write anything outside /tmp/corpus7/. Files to create (exact names): 1. ansible_playbook.yml — an Ansible playbook (2-3 plays, handlers, vars, loops, `when:` conditions, Jinja2 `{{ }}` templating in values, block/rescue, a multi-line `shell: |` script, some comments, some inconsistent spacing like `key: value`, a flow list). 2. changelog.md — a "Keep a Changelog"-style CHANGELOG with 6+ releases, nested bullet lists using `*` and `-`, long lines that would need re-wrapping, inline code, links, reference-style link definitions at the bottom, a few emphasis markers, an occasional numbered list. 3. contributing.md — a CONTRIBUTING guide: headings, numbered steps containing fenced code blocks (bash, yaml), a table, block quotes (including a GitHub alert like `> [!WARNING]`), nested lists, long paragraphs, an HTML comment, a `
` section. 4. docker_compose.yml — a docker-compose file with 5+ services, anchors and aliases (`x-common: &common`, `<<: *common`), environment as both list and mapping styles, healthchecks with flow sequences, long command strings, comments, profiles, volumes and networks sections. 5. github_workflow.yml — a GitHub Actions workflow with `on:` triggers (push with paths filters, pull_request, workflow_dispatch with inputs, schedule cron), concurrency, permissions, a matrix with include/exclude, steps using `${{ }}` expressions, multi-line `run: |` scripts, `if:` conditions. 6. kubernetes_multi_document.yaml — 4-6 Kubernetes manifests separated by `---` (Namespace, ConfigMap with a multi-line data value, Deployment with probes/resources/env/volumeMounts, Service, Ingress with annotations, HorizontalPodAutoscaler), with comments. 7. mkdocs_config.yml — an mkdocs.yml for Material theme: nav tree with nesting, theme features list, palette with toggles, markdown_extensions including ones with options and `!!python/name:` tags (e.g. `pymdownx.superfences` custom_fences with `format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format`), plugins, extra, copyright. 8. openapi.yaml — an OpenAPI 3.x spec with info (multi-line description using `|` with Markdown inside), servers, several paths with parameters, requestBody, responses, components/schemas with $ref, enums, examples, security schemes. 9. python_script.py — a realistic Python CLI script (argparse, dataclasses, logging, type hints), module docstring, function docstrings, and 2-3 strings or comment blocks preceded by a `# fmt: markdown` comment line on its own line directly above them (e.g. `# fmt: markdown` then `HELP_TEXT = """...markdown text with long lines, lists, emphasis..."""`, and a `# fmt: markdown` above a block of `#` comment lines containing Markdown). Use raw strings (r""") if the Markdown contains backslashes. 10. quarto_report.qmd — a Quarto report with YAML front matter (title, author list, format options, execute options), R or Python code chunks with `#|` options, callouts (`::: {.callout-note}`), cross-references, figures with captions, a table, footnotes, inline math and a display math block, long paragraphs. 11. r_script.R — a realistic R analysis script (library calls, functions, pipes, ggplot) including 2-3 places where a `# fmt: markdown` comment line on its own line sits directly above either a block of `#` comment lines containing Markdown, or an assignment of a multi-line string containing Markdown (e.g. `report_md <- "...` spanning several lines; avoid backslashes inside such non-raw strings, or use raw strings r"(...)"). 12. readme.md — a project README with badges (image links), a table of contents, installation instructions with fenced code, usage examples, a feature list, an FAQ section with nested lists, a license section, long paragraphs, a few HTML snippets (e.g. `

`). 13. rmarkdown_sentence_wrap.Rmd — an R Markdown document whose YAML front matter contains ``` editor_options: markdown: wrap: sentence ``` plus output options; prose paragraphs with multiple sentences per line (and some sentences split across lines), abbreviations like "e.g." and "et al.", citations like [@smith2020], R chunks with options, inline R code like `r nrow(df)`, a list, a table. Make them realistic and varied (real-world-looking content, 80-250 lines each), with natural imperfections people leave in such files: inconsistent indentation of nested lists, trailing spaces on some lines, long lines exceeding 100 characters, mixed bullet markers, extra blank lines, occasional tab characters in YAML comments is NOT allowed (YAML forbids tabs for indentation; keep YAML valid). All YAML files must be valid YAML. Use UTF-8 and LF line endings, except make changelog.md use CRLF line endings throughout. Reply with just the list of files written and their line counts.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

This session has no SendMessage tool, so it cannot message them with it; other sessions can still message this one. To reply, use your host application's own messaging tool if it provides one — otherwise a reply from here is not possible, and if one is needed, tell your user.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.

- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

---
# site.yml -- baseline + app deploy for the billing cluster
#
# Usage:
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/production/hosts.ini site.yml --limit webservers --diff
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml -e release_version=2.15.0-rc1 -e artifact_sha256=...
#
# NOTE(mk): run against staging first, the sshd template changed in March.

- name: Baseline configuration for all hosts
  hosts: all
  become: true
  gather_facts: yes

  vars:
    timezone: Europe/Berlin
    base_packages:
      - curl
      - git
      - htop
      - jq
      - vim-nox
      - unattended-upgrades
      - python3-pip
    admin_users:
      - { name: mkowalski, shell: /bin/bash, key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIOx2s7vB9dQk3hR mkowalski@thinkpad" }
      - { name: jdoe, shell: /bin/zsh, key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIK3p0QeW8hLrTzu jdoe@workstation" }
    sysctl_settings:
      net.core.somaxconn: 4096
      vm.swappiness:  10
      net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse: 1
      fs.file-max: 2097152

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Refresh apt cache if it is older than an hour
      apt:
        update_cache: yes
        cache_valid_time: 3600
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"

  tasks:
    - name: Install base packages
      package:
        name: "{{ item }}"
        state: present
      loop: "{{ base_packages }}"
      tags: [packages, baseline]

    - name: Set timezone
      community.general.timezone:
        name:  "{{ timezone }}"

    - name: Create admin users
      user:
        name: "{{ item.name }}"
        shell: "{{ item.shell }}"
        groups: sudo
        append: true
      loop: "{{ admin_users }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.name }}"

    - name: Install authorized keys for admins
      ansible.posix.authorized_key:
        user: "{{ item.name }}"
        key: "{{ item.key }}"
        exclusive: false
      loop: "{{ admin_users }}"
      loop_control:
          label: "{{ item.name }}"

    - name: Apply kernel tuning
      ansible.posix.sysctl:
        name: "{{ item.key }}"
        value: "{{ item.value }}"
        sysctl_file: /etc/sysctl.d/90-billing.conf
        reload: no
      loop: "{{ sysctl_settings | dict2items }}"
      when: not (running_in_container | default(false) | bool)
      notify: reload sysctl

    #- name: Disable IPv6 (breaks the old monitoring agent, see INFRA-2231)
    #  ansible.posix.sysctl:
    #    name: net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6
    #    value: "1"

    - name: Harden sshd
      template:
        src: templates/sshd_config.j2
        dest: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0600"
        validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
      notify:
        - restart sshd

  handlers:
    - name: reload sysctl
      command: sysctl --system

    - name: restart sshd
      service: name=ssh state=restarted


- name: Deploy billing-api
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  serial: "30%"
  max_fail_percentage: 10

  vars:
    app_name: billing-api
    app_user: billing
    app_root: /srv/{{ app_name }}
    release_version: "{{ lookup('env', 'RELEASE_VERSION') | default('2.14.1', true) }}"
    release_dir: "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ release_version }}"
    artifact_url: "https://artifacts.internal.example.com/repository/releases/{{ app_name }}/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz"
    # artifact_sha256 is passed in by the CI pipeline (-e artifact_sha256=...)
    keep_releases: 5
    healthcheck_url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz

  tasks:
    - name: Ensure application directories exist
      file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: directory
        owner: "{{ app_user }}"
        group: "{{ app_user }}"
        mode: "0755"
      loop:
        - "{{ app_root }}"
        - "{{ app_root }}/releases"
        - "{{ app_root }}/shared/log"
        - "{{ release_dir }}"

    - name: Deploy release
      block:
        - name: Download artifact
          get_url:
            url: "{{ artifact_url }}"
            dest: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            checksum: "sha256:{{ artifact_sha256 }}"
            timeout: 60

        - name: Unpack release
          unarchive:
            src: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            dest: "{{ release_dir }}"
            remote_src: yes
            owner: "{{ app_user }}"

        - name: Run database migrations (once per deploy)
          shell: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd {{ release_dir }}
            export $(grep -v '^#' {{ app_root }}/shared/.env | xargs)
            ./bin/migrate status || true
            ./bin/migrate up --lock-timeout 30s
            echo "$(date -Is) migrated to $(./bin/migrate version)" >> {{ app_root }}/shared/log/migrations.log
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash
          run_once: true
          become_user: "{{ app_user }}"
          register: migrate_result
          changed_when: "'no change' not in migrate_result.stdout"

        - name: Switch the current symlink
          file:
            src: "{{ release_dir }}"
            dest: "{{ app_root }}/current"
            state: link
            force: yes
          notify: restart billing-api

        - name: Flush handlers so the health check hits the new release
          meta: flush_handlers

        - name: Wait for the health check to pass
          uri:
            url: "{{ healthcheck_url }}"
            status_code: 200
            return_content: no
          register: health
          retries: 10
          delay: 3
          until: health.status == 200

      rescue:
        - name: Roll back to the previous release
          shell: |
            cd {{ app_root }}/releases
            prev=$(ls -1t | grep -vx '{{ release_version }}' | head -n 1)
            if [ -n "$prev" ]; then
              ln -sfn "{{ app_root }}/releases/$prev" {{ app_root }}/current
              systemctl restart {{ app_name }}
            fi
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash

        - name: Tell the team
          uri:
            url: "{{ slack_webhook_url }}"
            method: POST
            body_format: json
            body:
              text: ":rotating_light: deploy of {{ app_name }} {{ release_version }} failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}, rolled back"
          delegate_to: localhost
          become: false
          when: slack_webhook_url is defined

        - name: Fail the play
          fail:
            msg: "Deployment failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown error') }}"

      always:
        - name: Remove downloaded artifact
          file:
            path: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            state: absent

    - name: Prune old releases
      shell: ls -1dt {{ app_root }}/releases/* | tail -n +{{ keep_releases + 1 }} | xargs -r rm -rf
      changed_when: false

  handlers:
    - name: restart billing-api
      systemd:
        name: "{{ app_name }}"
        state: restarted
        daemon_reload: yes


- name: Nightly database backups
  hosts: dbservers
  become: yes
  vars:
    backup_dir: /var/backups/postgres
    backup_retention_days: 14
    databases: [billing, billing_audit, keycloak]
    s3_bucket: s3://acme-db-backups/{{ inventory_hostname_short }}

  tasks:
    - name: Install backup tooling
      apt:
        name: [postgresql-client-15, awscli, pigz]
        state: present

    - name: Create backup directory
      file: path={{ backup_dir }} state=directory owner=postgres group=postgres mode=0750

    - name: Install backup script

---
# site.yml -- baseline + app deploy for the billing cluster
#
# Usage:
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/production/hosts.ini site.yml --limit webservers --diff
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml -e release_version=2.15.0-rc1 -e artifact_sha256=...
#
# NOTE(mk): run against staging first, the sshd template changed in March.

- name: Baseline configuration for all hosts
  hosts: all
  become: true
  gather_facts: yes

  vars:
    timezone: Europe/Berlin
    base_packages:
      - curl
      - git
      - htop
      - jq
      - vim-nox
      - unattended-upgrades
      - python3-pip
    admin_users:
      - { name: mkowalski, shell: /bin/bash, key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIOx2s7vB9dQk3hR mkowalski@thinkpad" }
      - { name: jdoe, shell: /bin/zsh, key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIK3p0QeW8hLrTzu jdoe@workstation" }
    sysctl_settings:
      net.core.somaxconn: 4096
      vm.swappiness:  10
      net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse: 1
      fs.file-max: 2097152

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Refresh apt cache if it is older than an hour
      apt:
        update_cache: yes
        cache_valid_time: 3600
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"

  tasks:
    - name: Install base packages
      package:
        name: "{{ item }}"
        state: present
      loop: "{{ base_packages }}"
      tags: [packages, baseline]

    - name: Set timezone
      community.general.timezone:
        name:  "{{ timezone }}"

    - name: Create admin users
      user:
        name: "{{ item.name }}"
        shell: "{{ item.shell }}"
        groups: sudo
        append: true
      loop: "{{ admin_users }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.name }}"

    - name: Install authorized keys for admins
      ansible.posix.authorized_key:
        user: "{{ item.name }}"
        key: "{{ item.key }}"
        exclusive: false
      loop: "{{ admin_users }}"
      loop_control:
          label: "{{ item.name }}"

    - name: Apply kernel tuning
      ansible.posix.sysctl:
        name: "{{ item.key }}"
        value: "{{ item.value }}"
        sysctl_file: /etc/sysctl.d/90-billing.conf
        reload: no
      loop: "{{ sysctl_settings | dict2items }}"
      when: not (running_in_container | default(false) | bool)
      notify: reload sysctl

    #- name: Disable IPv6 (breaks the old monitoring agent, see INFRA-2231)
    #  ansible.posix.sysctl:
    #    name: net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6
    #    value: "1"

    - name: Harden sshd
      template:
        src: templates/sshd_config.j2
        dest: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0600"
        validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
      notify:
        - restart sshd

  handlers:
    - name: reload sysctl
      command: sysctl --system

    - name: restart sshd
      service: name=ssh state=restarted


- name: Deploy billing-api
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  serial: "30%"
  max_fail_percentage: 10

  vars:
    app_name: billing-api
    app_user: billing
    app_root: /srv/{{ app_name }}
    release_version: "{{ lookup('env', 'RELEASE_VERSION') | default('2.14.1', true) }}"
    release_dir: "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ release_version }}"
    artifact_url: "https://artifacts.internal.example.com/repository/releases/{{ app_name }}/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz"
    # artifact_sha256 is passed in by the CI pipeline (-e artifact_sha256=...)
    keep_releases: 5
    healthcheck_url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz

  tasks:
    - name: Ensure application directories exist
      file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: directory
        owner: "{{ app_user }}"
        group: "{{ app_user }}"
        mode: "0755"
      loop:
        - "{{ app_root }}"
        - "{{ app_root }}/releases"
        - "{{ app_root }}/shared/log"
        - "{{ release_dir }}"

    - name: Deploy release
      block:
        - name: Download artifact
          get_url:
            url: "{{ artifact_url }}"
            dest: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            checksum: "sha256:{{ artifact_sha256 }}"
            timeout: 60

        - name: Unpack release
          unarchive:
            src: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            dest: "{{ release_dir }}"
            remote_src: yes
            owner: "{{ app_user }}"

        - name: Run database migrations (once per deploy)
          shell: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd {{ release_dir }}
            export $(grep -v '^#' {{ app_root }}/shared/.env | xargs)
            ./bin/migrate status || true
            ./bin/migrate up --lock-timeout 30s
            echo "$(date -Is) migrated to $(./bin/migrate version)" >> {{ app_root }}/shared/log/migrations.log
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash
          run_once: true
          become_user: "{{ app_user }}"
          register: migrate_result
          changed_when: "'no change' not in migrate_result.stdout"

        - name: Switch the current symlink
          file:
            src: "{{ release_dir }}"
            dest: "{{ app_root }}/current"
            state: link
            force: yes
          notify: restart billing-api

        - name: Flush handlers so the health check hits the new release
          meta: flush_handlers

        - name: Wait for the health check to pass
          uri:
            url: "{{ healthcheck_url }}"
            status_code: 200
            return_content: no
          register: health
          retries: 10
          delay: 3
          until: health.status == 200

      rescue:
        - name: Roll back to the previous release
          shell: |
            cd {{ app_root }}/releases
            prev=$(ls -1t | grep -vx '{{ release_version }}' | head -n 1)
            if [ -n "$prev" ]; then
              ln -sfn "{{ app_root }}/releases/$prev" {{ app_root }}/current
              systemctl restart {{ app_name }}
            fi
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash

        - name: Tell the team
          uri:
            url: "{{ slack_webhook_url }}"
            method: POST
            body_format: json
            body:
              text: ":rotating_light: deploy of {{ app_name }} {{ release_version }} failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}, rolled back"
          delegate_to: localhost
          become: false
          when: slack_webhook_url is defined

        - name: Fail the play
          fail:
            msg: "Deployment failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown error') }}"

      always:
        - name: Remove downloaded artifact
          file:
            path: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            state: absent

    - name: Prune old releases
      shell: ls -1dt {{ app_root }}/releases/* | tail -n +{{ keep_releases + 1 }} | xargs -r rm -rf
      changed_when: false

  handlers:
    - name: restart billing-api
      systemd:
        name: "{{ app_name }}"
        state: restarted
        daemon_reload: yes


- name: Nightly database backups
  hosts: dbservers
  become: yes
  vars:
    backup_dir: /var/backups/postgres
    backup_retention_days: 14
    databases: [billing, billing_audit, keycloak]
    s3_bucket: s3://acme-db-backups/{{ inventory_hostname_short }}

  tasks:
    - name: Install backup tooling
      apt:
        name: [postgresql-client-15, awscli, pigz]
        state: present

    - name: Create backup directory
      file: path={{ backup_dir }} state=directory owner=postgres group=postgres mode=0750

    - name: Install backup script
      copy:
        dest: /usr/local/bin/pg-nightly-backup
        mode: "0755"
        content: |
          #!/usr/bin/env bash
          # Managed by Ansible -- local changes will be overwritten
          set -euo pipefail
          stamp=$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M)
          {% for db in databases %}
          pg_dump -Fc {{ db }} | pigz > {{ backup_dir }}/{{ db }}-${stamp}.dump.gz
          {% endfor %}
          aws s3 sync {{ backup_dir }} {{ s3_bucket }} --only-show-errors
          find {{ backup_dir }} -type f -name '*.dump.gz' -mtime +{{ backup_retention_days }} -delete

    - name: Schedule the backup
      cron:
        name: nightly pg backup
        user: postgres
        minute: "15"
        hour: "2"
        job: /usr/local/bin/pg-nightly-backup >> /var/log/pg-backup.log 2>&1
      when:
        - inventory_hostname == groups['dbservers'] | first
        - enable_backups | default(true) | bool

# Contributing to Fernwood

First off, thanks for taking the time to contribute! :tada: Fernwood is maintained by a handful of volunteers in their spare time, so every bug report, documentation fix and pull request genuinely helps.

This document describes how to set up a development environment, how we review changes and what we expect from a pull request. It is a living document -- if something here is outdated or unclear, please open an issue or (even better) a PR that fixes it. 

<!-- TODO(maintainers): move the release checklist into RELEASING.md once 3.0 is out -->

## Table of contents

- [Code of conduct](#code-of-conduct)
- [Reporting bugs](#reporting-bugs)
- [Development setup](#development-setup)
- [Running the test suite](#running-the-test-suite)
- [Style guide](#style-guide)
  - [Commit messages](#commit-messages)
- [Pull request process](#pull-request-process)
- [Releasing](#releasing)

## Code of conduct

This project follows the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/). By participating you are expected to uphold it. Please report unacceptable behaviour to conduct@fernwood.dev.

## Reporting bugs

Before opening a new issue, please search the [issue tracker](https://github.com/fernwood-dev/fernwood/issues) -- someone may already have reported the same problem. A good bug report contains:

* the Fernwood version (`python -c "import fernwood; print(fernwood.__version__)"`) and your Python version
* a **minimal** reproducible example. Ideally something we can paste into a REPL;
  screenshots of code are not very helpful.
* what you expected to happen, and what actually happened (including the full traceback)
   * if the problem only shows up with a particular schema, please include it
   * if it is a performance problem, the output of `python -m cProfile -s cumtime your_script.py | head -n 40` helps a lot

> [!NOTE]
> Security issues should **not** be reported in the public tracker. Please follow the instructions in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead.


## Development setup

Fernwood uses [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for dependency management, but plain `pip` + `venv` works just as well. You will need Python 3.9 or newer, and a C compiler if you want to build the optional speedups.

1. Fork the repository on GitHub and clone your fork:

   ```bash
   git clone git@github.com:<your-username>/fernwood.git
   cd fernwood
   git remote add upstream https://github.com/fernwood-dev/fernwood.git
   ```

2. Create a virtual environment and install the package in editable mode together with the development dependencies:

   ```bash
   uv venv --python 3.12
   source .venv/bin/activate
   uv pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"
   ```

3. Install the pre-commit hooks. They run `ruff`, `mypy` and a couple of sanity checks on every commit:

    ```bash
    pre-commit install
    pre-commit run --all-files   # optional, takes a minute the first time
    ```

4. (Optional) If you work on the C extension, set `FERNWOOD_BUILD_EXT=1` before installing. Our hook configuration looks roughly like this, in case you want to replicate it in your editor:

   ```yaml
   repos:
     - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
       rev: v0.6.9
       hooks:
         - id: ruff
           args: [--fix]
         - id: ruff-format
     - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-mypy
       rev: v1.11.2
       hooks:
         - id: mypy
           additional_dependencies: [types-python-dateutil]
   ```

> [!WARNING]
> Do not run `pip install fernwood` inside the development environment. It will shadow your editable install and you will spend an afternoon wondering why your changes have no effect (ask us how we know).

<details>
<summary>Notes for Windows users</summary>

The test suite runs on Windows in CI, but a few things work differently:

- activate the environment with `.venv\Scripts\activate` instead of `source`
- the speedups need the "Desktop development with C++" workload from the Visual Studio Build Tools
-   symlink-related tests are skipped unless Developer Mode is enabled

</details>

## Running the test suite

We use `pytest`. The quickest way to run everything is:

```bash
pytest -n auto
```

Some useful variations:

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `pytest tests/unit` | only the fast unit tests (< 10 s) |
| `pytest -m "not slow"` | skip the property-based tests that take several minutes |
| `pytest --cov=fernwood --cov-report=html` | coverage report in `htmlcov/` |
| `nox -s tests-3.9 tests-3.13` | run against several Python versions, like CI does |
| `nox -s docs` | build the documentation and fail on warnings |

If you add a new feature, please add tests for it. Bug fixes should come with a regression test that fails without the fix -- this is the single most useful thing you can do to make sure the bug stays fixed.

## Style guide

Formatting and linting are fully automated, so please don't spend time on manual formatting; `ruff format` is the source of truth. A few things the tools can't check:

- Public functions and classes need docstrings (Google style). Private helpers don't, but a one-line comment explaining *why* is always appreciated.
- Prefer small, focused modules. If a file grows beyond ~800 lines it is probably doing too much.
+ Type hints are required for all new code. We run `mypy --strict` on `src/`, but not on `tests/`.
- Error messages should say what went wrong **and** what the user can do about it, e.g. "field `age` must be >= 0, got -3" rather than "invalid value".

### Commit messages

We loosely follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). The type prefix is used to generate the changelog, so please get it right:

| Prefix | Use for | Shows up in changelog? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feat:` | new user-facing functionality | yes, under *Added* |
| `fix:` | bug fixes | yes, under *Fixed* |
| `perf:` | performance improvements | yes |
| `docs:` | documentation only | no |
| `refactor:` | code changes that neither fix a bug nor add a feature | no |
| `chore:` / `ci:` | tooling, dependencies, CI configuration | no |

Breaking changes must include a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer that explains the migration path.

## Pull request process

1. Open an issue first for anything bigger than a small bug fix, so we can agree on the approach before you invest a lot of time.
2. Keep pull requests focused. Two small PRs are much easier to review than one big one that does several unrelated things.
3. Make sure CI is green. If a check fails for reasons unrelated to your change (it happens, the macOS runners are flaky), leave a comment and a maintainer will re-run it.
4. Add a news fragment in `changes/`:
   - name it `<PR number>.<type>.md`, e.g. `1234.fixed.md`
   - one or two sentences, written for users rather than for reviewers
     * you can use Markdown, but keep it to inline formatting
5. A maintainer will review your PR, usually within a week. We may push small fixups directly to your branch, so please enable "Allow edits from maintainers".

> **Tip:** draft pull requests are welcome. Open one early if you want feedback on the general direction before polishing everything.

## Releasing

*This section is for maintainers.*

1. Make sure `main` is green and the changelog fragments look sensible: `towncrier build --draft`.
2. Bump the version and build the changelog:
   ```bash
   bump-my-version bump minor   # or patch / major
   towncrier build --yes
   git push upstream main --follow-tags
   ```
3. The `release` workflow builds the wheels and publishes them to PyPI via trusted publishing. Keep an eye on it, and if something goes wrong, **do not** delete the tag; yank the release on PyPI and cut a new patch version instead.



Thanks again for contributing!

# docker-compose.yml for local development of the shop stack.
#
#   docker compose up -d                          # core services
#   docker compose --profile monitoring up -d     # + prometheus/grafana
#   docker compose --profile debug up mailpit     # catch outgoing mail
#
# Copy .env.example to .env first, otherwise the api refuses to start.

name: shopfront

x-common: &common
  restart: unless-stopped
  logging:
    driver: json-file
    options:
      max-size: "10m"
      max-file: "3"
  networks:
    - backend

x-healthcheck: &healthcheck-defaults
  interval: 10s
  timeout: 5s
  retries: 5
  start_period: 20s

x-app-env: &app-env
  DATABASE_URL: postgres://shop:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-shop}@postgres:5432/shop
  REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
  CELERY_BROKER_URL: redis://redis:6379/1
  SECRET_KEY: ${SECRET_KEY:?SECRET_KEY must be set in .env}
  DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: shop.settings.local
  LOG_LEVEL:   ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}

services:
  traefik:
    <<: *common
    image: traefik:v3.1
    command:
      - --api.insecure=true
      - --providers.docker=true
      - --providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false
      - --entrypoints.web.address=:80
      - --accesslog=true
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "8081:8080"   # dashboard
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    networks:
      - frontend
      - backend

  web:
    <<: *common
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.dev
      args:
        NODE_VERSION: "20"
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=development
      - VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://api.shop.localhost
      - CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=true
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/app
      - web-node-modules:/app/node_modules
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.web.rule=Host(`shop.localhost`)"
      - "traefik.http.services.web.loadbalancer.server.port=5173"
    depends_on:
      - api
    networks: [frontend]

  api:
    <<: *common
    build: ./backend
    image: shopfront/api:dev
    command: >
      sh -c "python manage.py migrate --noinput &&
             python manage.py collectstatic --noinput --clear &&
             gunicorn shop.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 --workers 3 --threads 2 --timeout 120 --reload --access-logfile -"
    environment:
      <<: *app-env
      DJANGO_DEBUG: "true"
      ALLOWED_HOSTS: api.shop.localhost,localhost,127.0.0.1
    env_file: .env
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/srv/app
      - media:/srv/media
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`api.shop.localhost`)
      - traefik.http.services.api.loadbalancer.server.port=8000
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8000/healthz/ || exit 1"]

  worker:
    <<: *common
    image: shopfront/api:dev
    command: celery -A shop worker --loglevel=INFO --concurrency=4 --max-tasks-per-child=200 -Q default,emails,thumbnails
    environment:
      <<: *app-env
      C_FORCE_ROOT: "false"
    volumes:
      - ./backend:/srv/app
      - media:/srv/media
    depends_on: [api, redis]

  scheduler:
    <<: *common
    image: shopfront/api:dev
    command: celery -A shop beat --loglevel=INFO --scheduler django_celery_beat.schedulers:DatabaseScheduler
    environment: *app-env
    depends_on:
      - worker

  postgres:
    <<: *common
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: shop
      POSTGRES_USER: shop
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-shop}
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./docker/postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: [ "CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}" ]

  redis:
    <<: *common
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--maxmemory", "256mb", "--maxmemory-policy", "allkeys-lru"]
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      <<: *healthcheck-defaults
      test: [CMD, redis-cli, ping]
      interval: 5s

  # elasticsearch:
  #   image: docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:8.15.0
  #   environment:
  #     - discovery.type=single-node
  #     - xpack.security.enabled=false
  #   (search is mocked in dev for now, see SHOP-981)

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:latest
    profiles: ["debug"]
    ports:
      - "8025:8025"
      - "1025:1025"
    environment:
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY: 1
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE: 1
    networks:
      - backend

  prometheus:
    <<: *common
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.54.1
    profiles: [monitoring]
    command:
      - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=7d
    volumes:
      - ./docker/prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - prometheus-data:/prometheus

  grafana:
    <<: *common
    image: grafana/grafana:11.2.0
    profiles: [monitoring]
    environment:
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${GRAFANA_PASSWORD:-admin}
      GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP: "false"
    volumes:
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana
      - ./docker/grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
    depends_on: [prometheus]


volumes:
  pgdata:
  redis-data:
  media:
  web-node-modules:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-data:
    driver: local

networks:
  frontend:
  backend:
    driver: bridge
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.28.0.0/16

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - "release/**"
    tags: ["v*"]
    paths:
      - "src/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - pyproject.toml
      - requirements/*.txt
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
    paths-ignore:
      - "docs/**"
      - "**.md"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      debug_enabled:
        description: "Open a tmate session if a job fails (maintainers only)"
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false
      python-version:
        description: Python version for the lint job
        type: choice
        options: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
        default: "3.12"
      run-slow-tests:
        description: 'Also run tests marked with @pytest.mark.slow'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  schedule:
    # 03:17 UTC Mon-Fri; catches breakage caused by new releases of our dependencies
    - cron: "17 3 * * 1-5"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"
  PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK: 1
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED:  "1"

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint & type check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule' && !github.event.pull_request.draft
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version || '3.12' }}
          cache: pip
      - name: Install linters
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements/lint.txt
      - name: Ruff
        run: |
          ruff check --output-format=github .
          ruff format --check --diff .
      - name: Mypy
        run: mypy src/ --junit-xml reports/mypy.xml

  test:
    name: Test (${{ matrix.os }}, py${{ matrix.python-version }})
    needs: lint
    # also runs on schedule, where lint is skipped
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (needs.lint.result == 'success' || needs.lint.result == 'skipped') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-14, windows-latest]
        python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
        exclude:
          # the arm64 macOS runners don't ship 3.9
          - os: macos-14
            python-version: "3.9"
          - os: windows-latest
            python-version: "3.10"
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            python-version: "3.13"
            coverage: true
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            python-version: "3.14-dev"
            experimental: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0   # setuptools-scm needs the tags

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          allow-prereleases: true
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: |
            pyproject.toml
            requirements/*.txt

      - name: Install dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel
          python -m pip install -e ".[test]"
          if [ "${{ matrix.coverage }}" == "true" ]; then
            python -m pip install "coverage[toml]>=7.4" pytest-cov
          fi
          python -m pip list

      - name: Run tests
        shell: bash
        env:
          RUN_SLOW: ${{ (inputs.run-slow-tests || github.event_name == 'schedule') && '1' || '0' }}
        run: |
          markers="not slow and not flaky"
          if [ "$RUN_SLOW" = "1" ]; then markers="not flaky"; fi
          python -m pytest -n auto --durations=20 -m "$markers" \
            --junitxml=reports/junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}.xml \
            ${{ matrix.coverage && '--cov=fernwood --cov-branch --cov-report=xml' || '' }}

      - name: Upload coverage
        if: matrix.coverage && github.repository == 'fernwood-dev/fernwood'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: ./coverage.xml
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: false

      - name: Upload test results
        if: "!cancelled()"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: reports/*.xml
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Debug session
        if: ${{ failure() && inputs.debug_enabled }}
        uses: mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3
        with:
          limit-access-to-actor: true

  docs:
    name: Docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: lint
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'documentation')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: |
          python -m pip install -e ".[docs]"
          mkdocs build --strict --site-dir site/

  build:
    name: Build distributions
    needs: [test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package@v2

  publish:
    name: Publish to PyPI
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/project/fernwood/${{ github.ref_name }}
    permissions:
      id-token: write   # trusted publishing
      contents: write   # needed to create the GitHub release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Packages
          path: dist
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
      - name: Create GitHub release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release create "${{ github.ref_name }}" dist/* \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --title "Fernwood ${{ github.ref_name }}" \
            --notes "See the [changelog](https://fernwood.readthedocs.io/en/stable/changelog.html) for details." \
            --verify-tag

# orders-service -- production manifests
# Synced by Argo CD from platform-config/apps/orders; please don't kubectl apply by hand.
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: orders
  labels:
    team: checkout
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: orders-service-config
  namespace: orders
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: orders-service
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: checkout
data:
  LOG_FORMAT: json
  FEATURE_FLAGS: "split-shipments,async-invoices"
  application.yaml: |
    server:
      port: 8080
      shutdown: graceful
    spring:
      lifecycle:
        timeout-per-shutdown-phase: 25s
      datasource:
        url: jdbc:postgresql://orders-db.orders.svc.cluster.local:5432/orders?sslmode=require
        hikari:
          maximum-pool-size: 20
          connection-timeout: 3000
      kafka:
        bootstrap-servers: kafka-0.kafka-headless.messaging:9092,kafka-1.kafka-headless.messaging:9092
        consumer:
          group-id: orders-service
    management:
      server:
        port: 8081
      endpoints:
        web:
          exposure:
            include: health,info,prometheus
---
# The digest is bumped by the release pipeline; the tag is only there for humans.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: orders-service
  namespace: orders
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: orders-service
    app.kubernetes.io/version: "3.18.2"
  annotations:
    # bump this to force a rollout when only the ConfigMap changed
    checkout.example.com/config-revision: "14"
spec:
  replicas: 3
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: orders-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: orders-service
        app.kubernetes.io/version: "3.18.2"
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "8081"
        prometheus.io/path: /actuator/prometheus
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: orders-service
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 40
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        fsGroup: 10001
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: orders-service
      containers:
        - name: orders-service
          image: registry.example.com/checkout/orders-service:3.18.2@sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
            - name: management
              containerPort: 8081
          env:
            - name: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
              value: prod,kubernetes
            - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
              value: "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8"
            - name: SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: orders-db-credentials
                  key: username
            - name: SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef: {name: orders-db-credentials, key: password}
            - name: POD_NAME
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef: {fieldPath: metadata.name}
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 768Mi
            limits:
              memory: 1Gi     # no CPU limit on purpose, see PLAT-311
          startupProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /actuator/health/liveness, port: management}
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 30
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /actuator/health/liveness
              port: management
            periodSeconds: 10
            timeoutSeconds: 2
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /actuator/health/readiness
              port: management
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 3
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 10"]
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /workspace/config
              readOnly: true
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: orders-service-config
            items:
              - key: application.yaml
                path: application.yaml
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir:
            sizeLimit: 256Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: orders-service
  namespace: orders
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: orders-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: orders-service
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: http
  - name: management
    port: 8081
