---
title: "Urban green space and self-reported wellbeing"
subtitle: "Secondary analysis of the 2023 Neighbourhood Health Survey"
author:
  - "Jide Okafor"
  - "Lena Brandt"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
  bookdown::html_document2:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    number_sections: true
    df_print: paged
    code_folding: hide
  bookdown::pdf_document2:
    latex_engine: xelatex
    keep_tex: false
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl
link-citations: true
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(broom.mixed)
library(knitr)

nhs <- read_rds("data/nhs2023_clean.rds")
```

# Background

Access to green space has been linked to better mental health in a large number of observational studies [@smith2020; @lee2021]. Most of this work, however, relies on fairly crude exposure measures,
e.g. the share of green land use within an administrative area, which says little about whether residents actually use the space. Markevych et al. [-@markevych2017] proposed a framework with three pathways: mitigation (e.g. reduced noise and air pollution), restoration, and instoration (i.e. encouraging physical activity and social contact).
In this report we look at whether *distance to the nearest park* and *park size* are associated with wellbeing once the usual socio-economic confounders are taken into account.

The analysis was pre-registered in March 2024. Deviations from the pre-registered plan are listed in Section \@ref(deviations).

# Data

We use the 2023 wave of the Neighbourhood Health Survey (NHS), a postal and online survey of adults living in the 14 districts of the city. After excluding respondents with missing outcome data, the analytic sample contains `r nrow(nhs)` people in `r n_distinct(nhs$lsoa)` small areas.
Wellbeing is measured with the Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale (WEMWBS), which ranges from 14 to 70 [@tennant2007]. The sample mean was `r round(mean(nhs$wemwbs, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` (SD `r round(sd(nhs$wemwbs, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`), slightly above the national average reported by
the ONS for 2022.

Exposure variables were derived from the city's open data portal (approx. 1,100 parks and green spaces, as of Jan. 2024):

- `park_dist_m`: network distance in metres from the respondent's postcode centroid to the nearest park entrance.
- `park_area_ha`: area of that park in hectares.
- `green_share`: share of green land use within 500 m, as used by most previous studies (cf. Dr. Patel's 2019 report for the council).
    - This is the *only* exposure that is also available for the 2019 wave.

```{r descriptives}
nhs %>%
  group_by(district) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    wemwbs = mean(wemwbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    dist = median(park_dist_m),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(wemwbs)) %>%
  kable(digits = 1, col.names = c("District", "n", "Mean WEMWBS", "Median distance (m)"))
```

# Methods

We fitted linear mixed models with a random intercept for small area (LSOA). Covariates were chosen a priori: age, sex, household income (quintiles), employment status, self-rated general health, and years at the current address. Distance was log-transformed because the relationship was clearly non-linear in exploratory plots (see Fig. \@ref(fig:dist-plot)). All models were fitted in R `r getRversion()` with lme4 [@bates2015].

```{r models, cache=TRUE}
m0 <- lmer(wemwbs ~ age + sex + income_q + employment + health + years_at_address + (1 | lsoa), data = nhs)
m1 <- update(m0, . ~ . + log(park_dist_m))
m2 <- update(m1, . ~ . + log(park_area_ha))
m3 <- update(m0, . ~ . + green_share)
```

```{r dist-plot, fig.cap="WEMWBS score by distance to the nearest park. Points are jittered vertically; the line is a LOESS smooth with 95% CI.", fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
ggplot(nhs, aes(park_dist_m, wemwbs)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.15, width = 0, height = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = "darkgreen") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Distance to nearest park (m, log scale)", y = "WEMWBS")
```

# Results

Table \@ref(tab:coef-table) shows the main estimates. Each doubling of the distance to the nearest park was associated with a `r abs(round(fixef(m1)[["log(park_dist_m)"]] * log(2), 2))` point lower WEMWBS score.
This is small compared with, e.g., the gap between the lowest and highest income quintile (approx. 4 points), but comparable to the effects reported by Jones et al. (2019) and by @brown2018 for a similar population. The association with park size was weaker, and its confidence interval included zero.

| Model | Exposure            | Estimate | 95% CI         |
|-------|---------------------|---------:|----------------|
| M1    | log distance        | -0.52    | -0.81 to -0.23 |
| M2 | log distance + log area | -0.47 | -0.77 to -0.17 |
| M3    | green share (per 10 pp) | 0.21 | -0.02 to 0.44 |

Results were robust to excluding respondents who had moved in the last year (n = 412) and to using the short 7-item version of the scale (SWEMWBS) instead of the full one. Further sensitivity analyses are in the supplementary material, Sect. S2.

```{r coef-table}
list(M1 = m1, M2 = m2, M3 = m3) %>%
  map_dfr(~ tidy(.x, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE), .id = "model") %>%
  filter(str_detect(term, "park|green")) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Fixed effects for the exposure variables.")
```

# Deviations from the pre-registration {#deviations}

1. We pre-registered a Poisson model for the number of park visits as a secondary outcome. The visit question was changed between survey waves, so this analysis was dropped.
2. The covariate "years at current address" was added after comments from an internal reviewer (Dr. A. Novak, pers. comm.).
   It was not part of the original plan.
3. We used `lme4` instead of `nlme` because the latter did not converge for the M2 vs. M0 comparison. Estimates from the models that did converge in both packages agreed to the second decimal place.

# References

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prune old backup archives according to a grandfather-father-son policy.

The script walks a backup directory, parses the timestamp embedded in every
archive name and deletes whatever is not covered by the retention policy.
It is meant to run from cron right after the nightly backup job, e.g.::

    15 4 * * *  /opt/tools/prune_backups.py /srv/backups --keep-daily 7 --apply

Nothing is deleted unless ``--apply`` is given.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Sequence

__version__ = "1.4.0"

log = logging.getLogger("prune_backups")

# db-billing-2024-03-18T021500.tar.zst, home-2024-03-18T021500.tar.gz, ...
ARCHIVE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<prefix>[\w.-]+?)-(?P<stamp>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T\d{6})"
    r"\.(?P<ext>tar(?:\.(?:gz|zst|xz))?|dump)$"
)
STAMP_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%S"

# fmt: markdown
EPILOG = """
Retention policy
----------------

An archive is kept if it falls into *any* of the configured buckets:

* one of the newest `--keep-daily` days that have at least one archive,
* one of the newest `--keep-weekly` ISO weeks (only the **last** archive of each week is kept),
    * weeks run Monday to Sunday, in local time
* one of the newest `--keep-monthly` months.

Everything else is a deletion candidate. Without `--apply` the script only prints what it would do, which is the default because deleting backups by accident is the kind of mistake you only make once.

Examples:

1. Preview with the default policy: `prune_backups.py /srv/backups`
2. Two weeks of dailies and a year of monthlies:
   `prune_backups.py /srv/backups --keep-daily 14 --keep-monthly 12 --apply`
"""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Archive:
    """A single backup archive found on disk."""

    path: Path
    prefix: str
    taken_at: datetime
    size: int

    @property
    def day(self) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
        return (self.taken_at.year, self.taken_at.month, self.taken_at.day)

    @property
    def week(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        iso = self.taken_at.isocalendar()
        return (iso[0], iso[1])

    @property
    def month(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        return (self.taken_at.year, self.taken_at.month)


@dataclass
class Policy:
    keep_daily: int = 7
    keep_weekly: int = 4
    keep_monthly: int = 6
    min_age: timedelta = timedelta(hours=12)


@dataclass
class Plan:
    keep: dict[Path, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    prune: list[Archive] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def reclaimed_bytes(self) -> int:
        return sum(a.size for a in self.prune)


def scan(root: Path, prefixes: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> list[Archive]:
    """Return all archives below *root*, newest first.

    Files that do not match :data:`ARCHIVE_RE` are skipped with a debug message,
    so it is safe to keep checksums or log files next to the archives.
    """
    archives: list[Archive] = []
    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        m = ARCHIVE_RE.match(path.name)
        if m is None:
            log.debug("skipping %s: name does not look like an archive", path)
            continue
        if prefixes and m["prefix"] not in prefixes:
            continue
        taken_at = datetime.strptime(m["stamp"], STAMP_FORMAT)
        archives.append(Archive(path, m["prefix"], taken_at, path.stat().st_size))
    archives.sort(key=lambda a: a.taken_at, reverse=True)
    return archives


# fmt: markdown
# ## How buckets are assigned
#
# For every archive we compute three keys: the calendar *day*, the ISO *week* `(year, week)` and the *month* `(year, month)`. Within a bucket only the newest archive survives, so a weekly slot never keeps two archives from the same week.
#
# 1. Sort the archives newest first (done in `scan`).
# 2. Walk the list and fill the daily, weekly and monthly slots until each policy is exhausted.
#    - one archive may occupy several slots
#       - e.g. the Sunday backup is usually both a daily *and* a weekly
# 3. Anything that never got a slot is pruned.
#
# `--min-age` is checked **after** this, so very fresh archives are never deleted, even when the policy says so.
def plan_retention(archives: Iterable[Archive], policy: Policy, now: datetime) -> Plan:
    plan = Plan()
    buckets = (
        ("daily", policy.keep_daily, lambda a: a.day),
        ("weekly", policy.keep_weekly, lambda a: a.week),
        ("monthly", policy.keep_monthly, lambda a: a.month),
    )
    archives = list(archives)
    for name, limit, key in buckets:
        seen: set[tuple[int, ...]] = set()
        for archive in archives:
            if len(seen) >= limit:
                break
            k = key(archive)
            if k in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(k)
            plan.keep.setdefault(archive.path, []).append(name)

    for archive in archives:
        if archive.path in plan.keep:
            continue
        if now - archive.taken_at < policy.min_age:
            plan.keep[archive.path] = ["too-young"]
            continue
        plan.prune.append(archive)
    return plan


# fmt: markdown
SUMMARY_TEMPLATE = r"""
### Pruning report for `{root}`

| bucket | kept |
|---|---:|
| daily | {daily} |
| weekly   | {weekly} |
| monthly | {monthly} |
| **pruned** | {pruned} ({reclaimed}) |

Windows hosts keep their archives under `D:\Backups\{host}`; remember to escape the backslashes (`D:\\Backups`) in `prune.toml`.
Files ending in \*.partial are never touched.
"""


def human_size(n: float) -> str:
    for unit in ("B", "KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB"):
        if n < 1024 or unit == "TiB":
            return f"{n:.1f} {unit}" if unit != "B" else f"{int(n)} B"
        n /= 1024
    raise AssertionError("unreachable")


def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="prune_backups.py",
        description="Delete old backup archives according to a retention policy.",
        epilog=EPILOG,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    parser.add_argument("root", type=Path, help="directory that contains the archives")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-daily", type=int, default=7, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-weekly", type=int, default=4, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-monthly", type=int, default=6, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--min-age-hours", type=float, default=12.0,
                        help="never delete archives younger than this (default: %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument("--prefix", action="append", dest="prefixes",
                        help="only consider archives with this prefix; may be repeated")
    parser.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true", help="actually delete files")
    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path, help="write a Markdown summary to this file")
    parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"%(prog)s {__version__}")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.WARNING - 10 * min(args.verbose, 2),
        format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)-7s %(message)s",
    )

    if not args.root.is_dir():
        log.error("%s is not a directory", args.root)
        return 2

    policy = Policy(args.keep_daily, args.keep_weekly, args.keep_monthly,
                    timedelta(hours=args.min_age_hours))
    archives = scan(args.root, args.prefixes)
    if not archives:
        log.warning("no archives found below %s", args.root)
        return 0

    plan = plan_retention(archives, policy, now=datetime.now())
    for path, reasons in sorted(plan.keep.items()):
        log.info("keep   %s (%s)", path, ", ".join(reasons))
    for archive in plan.prune:
        if args.apply:
            log.warning("delete %s", archive.path)
            try:
                archive.path.unlink()
            except OSError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the filesystem
                log.error("could not delete %s: %s", archive.path, exc)
        else:
            print(f"would delete {archive.path}")

    if args.report:
        counts = {name: sum(name in r for r in plan.keep.values()) for name in ("daily", "weekly", "monthly")}
        args.report.write_text(SUMMARY_TEMPLATE.format(
            root=args.root, host="<host>", pruned=len(plan.prune),
            reclaimed=human_size(plan.reclaimed_bytes), **counts,
        ))
    log.info("%d archives, %d to prune, %s reclaimable", len(archives), len(plan.prune), human_size(plan.reclaimed_bytes))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

title: "Customer churn, Q3 2024"
subtitle: "Why monthly subscribers leave, and what we can do about it"

date: 2024-10-14
date-format: long
abstract: |
  Monthly churn among self-serve subscribers rose from 3.1% in June to 4.4% in September 2024. This report breaks the increase down by plan, acquisition channel and tenure, and estimates how much of it is explained by the August price change.
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    number-sections: true
    code-fold: true
    code-tools: true
    theme: [cosmo, custom.scss]
    fig-width: 8

    documentclass: scrartcl
    papersize: a4

      - margin=2.2cm

  echo: false

---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
library(gt)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

subs <- read_csv(here::here("data", "subscriptions_2024q3.csv"),
                 col_types = cols(plan = col_factor(), channel = col_factor()))

churn_monthly <- subs |>
  mutate(month = floor_date(period_start, "month")) |>
  group_by(month, plan) |>
  summarise(active = n(), churned = sum(cancelled), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(rate = churned / active)
```

## Summary

::: {.callout-note}
## TL;DR
Churn went up in **every** plan, but the jump is concentrated in the *Starter* plan after the price change on 1 August. Annual plans are essentially unaffected.
:::

Between June and September the share of monthly subscribers who cancelled within a given month went from 3.1% to 4.4% (@fig-monthly-churn). Most of the increase comes from customers in their first three months, who are also the group most exposed to the new pricing page; customers with more than a year of tenure churned at roughly the same rate as before. We estimate that the price change explains about two thirds of the increase, with the remainder attributable to a seasonal effect that we also saw, in weaker form, in 2023[^seasonality].

[^seasonality]: The 2023 data uses the old plan structure, so the comparison is only approximate. See the appendix of last year's report for the mapping between old and new plans.

## Data

We use the subscription ledger exported on 2 October 2024. A subscription counts as *active* in a month if it was active on the first day of that month, and as *churned* if it was cancelled by the customer before the first day of the next month.
Prices before and after the change are listed in @tbl-plans.

::: {.callout-warning}
Involuntary churn (failed payments) is **excluded** throughout. It accounts for roughly 0.6 percentage points per month and is tracked separately by the billing team.
:::

| Plan     | Price before | Price after | Active subs (Sept) |
|:---------|-------------:|------------:|-------------------:|
| Starter  | €9           | €12         | 18,402 |
| Team | €29 | €29 | 6,117 |
| Business     | €79          | €89         | 1,230              |

: Plans and monthly prices. Annual plans are billed at ten times the monthly price. {#tbl-plans}

## Methods

We model the time to cancellation with a Cox proportional hazards model,

$$
\lambda(t \mid x) = \lambda_0(t) \exp\left(\beta_1 \,\text{plan} + \beta_2 \,\text{channel} + \beta_3 \,\text{post}_t\right)
$$ {#eq-cox}

where $\text{post}_t$ indicates observation months after the price change and $\lambda_0(t)$ is the baseline hazard. The coefficient of interest is $\beta_3$: $\exp(\beta_3) > 1$ means that customers were more likely to cancel after the change. Tenure is the time axis, so the model compares customers at the same point in their lifecycle, which matters because new customers churn at a much higher rate than established ones regardless of price.

```{r}
#| label: fit-cox
#| cache: true
fit <- coxph(
  Surv(tenure_days, cancelled) ~ plan + channel + post_change + strata(cohort),
  data = subs
)
```

## Results

```{r}
#| label: fig-monthly-churn
#| fig-cap: "Monthly churn rate by plan. The dashed line marks the price change on 1 August 2024."
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the monthly churn rate for the Starter, Team and Business plans, January to September 2024."
ggplot(churn_monthly, aes(month, rate, colour = plan)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.Date("2024-08-01"), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Monthly churn", colour = "Plan")
```

@fig-monthly-churn shows that the Starter plan accounts for almost all of the increase. The hazard ratios for the post-change period and the other covariates are in @tbl-cox; as described in @eq-cox, all estimates are conditional on tenure.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cox
#| tbl-cap: "Hazard ratios from the Cox model, with 95% confidence intervals."
broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = p.value, decimals = 1)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Robustness checks
- Excluding customers acquired through the July partner promotion changes $\hat\beta_3$ by less than 0.02.
- Using calendar time instead of tenure as the time axis gives a hazard ratio of 1.38 instead of 1.41.
   - the proportional hazards assumption looks fine for plan and channel (Schoenfeld residuals, see appendix)
* A simple difference-in-differences against annual subscribers gives a similar result.
:::

![Cancellation reasons selected in the exit survey, September 2024.](figures/exit-survey.png){#fig-exit-survey width=80%}

The exit survey (@fig-exit-survey) supports this reading: "too expensive" was the most frequently selected reason in September (41% of responses, up from 27% in June), while "missing features" stayed flat at around 15%.


## Recommendations

1. Re-introduce a cheaper Starter tier for the first three months, and measure the effect with a proper holdout group this time.
2. Move the price-change email out of the first week of the billing cycle, when customers are most likely to review their subscriptions anyway.
3. Track involuntary churn in the same dashboard, so that the two numbers are not confused again[^dunning].

[^dunning]: See the billing team's dunning analysis from August for details on the payment-failure side.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# bikeshare_weekly.R
#
# Weekly usage report for the city bike-share scheme. Reads the raw trip export
# from the operator's SFTP drop, cleans it and writes a Markdown summary plus a
# couple of charts to output/<iso-week>/.
#
# Author: M. Lindqvist      Last touched: 2024-10-02
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
  library(glue)
})

# fmt: markdown
# ## What this script does
#
# 1. Load the trip exports (`trips_YYYYMMDD.csv.gz`) for the last **complete** ISO week.
# 2. Drop obviously broken records:
#    * trips shorter than 60 seconds (docking glitches) or longer than 24 hours,
#    * trips whose start or end station is not listed in `stations.csv`.
# 3. Summarise trips per day, per station and per user type.
# 4. Write the charts and a Markdown summary into `output/<week>/`, which the comms team picks up every Monday morning for the newsletter.
#
# Run it as `Rscript bikeshare_weekly.R 2024-W39`, or without arguments to report on last week.

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
week_arg <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else NA_character_

data_dir   <- Sys.getenv("BIKESHARE_DATA", "data/raw")
output_dir<-"output"


# ---- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Parse an ISO week like "2024-W39" into the Monday of that week.
# Without an argument we report on the last complete week.
iso_week_start <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x)) {
    return(floor_date(today() - weeks(1), unit = "week", week_start = 1))
  }
  parts <- regmatches(x, regexec("^([0-9]{4})-W([0-9]{2})$", x))[[1]]
  if (length(parts) != 3) stop("week must look like 2024-W39, got: ", x, call. = FALSE)
  jan4 <- as.Date(paste0(parts[2], "-01-04"))
  floor_date(jan4, "week", week_start = 1) + weeks(as.integer(parts[3]) - 1)
}

read_trips <- function(path) {
  read_csv(
    path,
    col_types = cols(
      trip_id       = col_character(),
      started_at    = col_datetime(),
      ended_at      = col_datetime(),
      start_station = col_integer(),
      end_station   = col_integer(),
      user_type     = col_factor(levels = c("member", "casual")),
      bike_type = col_character()
    ),
    progress = FALSE
  )
}

clean_trips <- function(trips, stations) {
  n_before <- nrow(trips)
  out <- trips %>%
    mutate(duration_min = as.numeric(difftime(ended_at, started_at, units = "mins"))) %>%
    filter(between(duration_min, 1, 24 * 60)) %>%
    semi_join(stations, by = c("start_station" = "station_id")) %>%
    semi_join(stations, by = c("end_station" = "station_id"))
  message(sprintf("dropped %d of %d trips (%.1f%%)", n_before - nrow(out), n_before,
                  100 * (n_before - nrow(out)) / n_before))
  out
}

# ---- load -------------------------------------------------------------------

week_start <- iso_week_start(week_arg)
week_end   <- week_start + days(6)
week_label <- strftime(week_start, "%G-W%V")

stations <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "stations.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

day_files <- file.path(data_dir, strftime(seq(week_start, week_end, by = "day"), "trips_%Y%m%d.csv.gz"))
missing <- day_files[!file.exists(day_files)]
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  warning("missing exports: ", paste(basename(missing), collapse = ", "))
}

trips <- day_files[file.exists(day_files)] |>
  lapply(read_trips) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  clean_trips(stations)

# ---- summarise --------------------------------------------------------------

daily <- trips %>%
  mutate(day = as_date(started_at)) %>%
  count(day, user_type, name = "trips") %>%
  complete(day = seq(week_start, week_end, by = "day"), user_type, fill = list(trips = 0))

top_stations <- trips %>%
  count(start_station, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  left_join(stations, by = c("start_station" = "station_id"))

summary_stats <- trips %>%
  summarise(
    n_trips      = n(),
    median_min   = median(duration_min),
    share_ebike  = mean(bike_type == "electric"),
    share_member = mean(user_type == "member")
  )

# ---- plots ------------------------------------------------------------------

p_daily <- ggplot(daily, aes(x = day, y = trips, fill = user_type)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.8) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%a %d %b", date_breaks = "1 day") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(member = "#1b9e77", casual = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = glue("Trips per day, {week_label}"), x = NULL, y = "Trips", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

p_duration <- trips %>%
  filter(duration_min <= 90) %>%
  ggplot(aes(duration_min, after_stat(density), colour = user_type)) +
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~bike_type) +
  labs(x = "Trip duration (minutes)", y = NULL, colour = NULL)

week_dir <- file.path(output_dir, week_label)
dir.create(week_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave(file.path(week_dir, "trips_per_day.png"), p_daily, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
ggsave(file.path(week_dir, "duration.png"), p_duration, width = 8, height = 4, dpi = 150)

# ---- report -----------------------------------------------------------------

# fmt: markdown
report_md <- "# Bike-share weekly report: {week_label}

Between {format(week_start, '%d %B')} and {format(week_end, '%d %B %Y')} riders took **{comma(summary_stats$n_trips)} trips**. The median trip lasted {round(summary_stats$median_min, 1)} minutes and {percent(summary_stats$share_ebike, accuracy = 1)} of all trips were made on e-bikes.

* members made {percent(summary_stats$share_member, accuracy = 1)} of the trips
* the busiest station was *{top_stations$name[1]}* with {comma(top_stations$n[1])} departures
   * followed by *{top_stations$name[2]}* ({comma(top_stations$n[2])})
- charts: `trips_per_day.png`, `duration.png`

![Trips per day](trips_per_day.png)
"

writeLines(glue(report_md), file.path(week_dir, "README.md"))

# fmt: markdown
methods_md <- r"(
## Methods and caveats

Trip durations are computed as `ended_at - started_at`. Records shorter than one minute or longer than $24 \times 60$ minutes are dropped as docking errors. Station names come from `stations.csv` as of the report date, so renamed stations show their **new** name for historical weeks too.

Known issues:

1. The operator's export double-counts trips that cross midnight on DST change days.
2. E-bike share is based on `bike_type`, which is missing for about 2% of trips before March 2024; those are counted as classic bikes.
)"
cat(methods_md, file = file.path(week_dir, "README.md"), append = TRUE)

message("report written to ", normalizePath(week_dir))

Driftwood

Catch database schema drift before your next migration does.
Documentation · Discussions · Changelog

[![CI](https://github.com/driftwood-db/driftwood/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/driftwood-db/driftwood/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/driftwood-db/driftwood/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/driftwood-db/driftwood) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/driftwood-db.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/driftwood-db/) [![Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/driftwood-db.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/driftwood-db/) [![Docker pulls](https://img.shields.io/docker/pulls/driftwood/driftwood)](https://hub.docker.com/r/driftwood/driftwood) [![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) Driftwood compares the schema of a live PostgreSQL or MySQL database with the schema your migration files *say* it should have, and tells you exactly where the two disagree. It was born out of one too many incidents where somebody "just quickly" added an index in production, the next deploy's migration failed at 2am, and nobody could tell which of the forty differences between staging and production actually mattered. Driftwood is **read-only** by design: it never modifies the database it inspects. ## Table of contents - [Features](#features) - [Installation](#installation) - [pip / pipx](#pip--pipx) - [Docker](#docker) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Using Driftwood in CI](#using-driftwood-in-ci) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) ## Features - **Two-way diff** between a live database and the schema you get by replaying your migrations into a throwaway container - Understands Alembic, Django, Flyway and Liquibase migrations (XML and YAML changelogs), as well as plain directories of numbered `.sql` files * Ignore rules for objects you don't care about, e.g. `pg_stat_statements` views, temp tables or partitions created by `pg_partman` * Output as human-readable text, JSON, JUnit XML or a GitHub Actions job summary - Generates a *suggested* fix migration. Review it before you run it -- Driftwood can't know whether a missing column should be added or the migration that created it should be deleted - Fast: diffing a 1,200-table schema takes about three seconds, most of which is spent waiting for `pg_dump` ## Installation Driftwood requires Python 3.9+ and, for the migration replay, a running Docker daemon (Podman works too if the Docker-compatible socket is enabled). ### pip / pipx ```bash pipx install driftwood-db # or, inside an existing virtualenv: pip install "driftwood-db[postgres,mysql]" ``` ### Docker ```bash docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/project" -w /project \ -e DRIFTWOOD_DSN="postgresql://readonly@db.internal:5432/app" \ ghcr.io/driftwood-db/driftwood:latest check ``` The image ships `pg_dump` 12 through 17 and `mysqldump` 8.0/8.4 and picks the right one based on the server version. ## Quick start 1. Point Driftwood at your migrations and your database: ```bash driftwood init --migrations alembic/versions --dsn "$DATABASE_URL" ``` 2. Run a check: ```console $ driftwood check Replaying 214 migrations into postgres:16 ... done (41.2s) Comparing with db.internal:5432/app ... ~ table public.orders + index orders_created_at_idx (created_at) only in live database ~ column status: varchar(20) -> varchar(32) type differs - table public.legacy_coupons only in migrations 3 differences (1 error, 2 warnings) ``` 3. Decide what to do about each difference: either write a migration, or add an ignore rule if the difference is intentional. ## Configuration Driftwood reads `driftwood.yml` from the current directory (or the `[tool.driftwood]` table in `pyproject.toml`, if you prefer): ```yaml migrations: tool: alembic path: alembic/versions database: dsn: ${DATABASE_URL} schemas: [public, billing] ignore: - kind: index name: "*_tmp_idx" - kind: table schema: public name: django_session # recreated by a cron job, see OPS-412 severity: extra_index: warning missing_column: error ``` Every option can also be set through environment variables, e.g. `DRIFTWOOD_DATABASE__DSN`. Environment variables take precedence over the config file, which in turn takes precedence over the built-in defaults. ## Using Driftwood in CI The most common setup is a nightly job that runs `driftwood check --format github` against a read replica and fails if there are any errors. The `github` format writes a job summary with a collapsible diff per table, so you can see at a glance what changed without digging through the logs.
Example GitHub Actions workflow ```yaml name: schema-drift on: schedule: - cron: "0 5 * * *" jobs: drift: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - run: pipx run driftwood-db check --format github env: DRIFTWOOD_DSN: ${{ secrets.REPLICA_DSN }} ```
## FAQ **Does Driftwood ever write to my database?** No. It only needs a role that can read the catalog. We recommend creating a dedicated read-only role: - PostgreSQL: membership in `pg_read_all_stats` is enough for most setups - MySQL: `SELECT` on `information_schema` plus `SHOW VIEW` on the schemas you want to check * on MySQL 5.7 you also need `PROCESS`, otherwise some index metadata is hidden **Why does it need Docker?** To know what the schema *should* look like, Driftwood replays your migrations into an empty database of the same major version. Doing that in a container is the only reliable way we found to match production exactly, including extensions, collations and server defaults. **Can I compare two live databases without any migrations?** Yes: `driftwood diff postgresql://staging/app postgresql://prod/app`. This skips the replay step entirely. **What about other kinds of objects?** - stored procedures and functions: compared by a normalised hash of the body, so whitespace-only changes are ignored - views: same as functions - row-level security policies: supported on PostgreSQL 13+ - policies on partitioned tables are only compared on the parent ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are very welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first; it explains how to run the test suite (which needs Docker, too) and how releases work.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(broom.mixed)
library(knitr)

nhs <- read_rds("data/nhs2023_clean.rds")
```

# Background

Access to green space has been linked to better mental health in a large number of observational studies [@smith2020; @lee2021]. Most of this work, however, relies on fairly crude exposure measures,
e.g. the share of green land use within an administrative area, which says little about whether residents actually use the space. Markevych et al. [-@markevych2017] proposed a framework with three pathways: mitigation (e.g. reduced noise and air pollution), restoration, and instoration (i.e. encouraging physical activity and social contact).
In this report we look at whether *distance to the nearest park* and *park size* are associated with wellbeing once the usual socio-economic confounders are taken into account.

The analysis was pre-registered in March 2024. Deviations from the pre-registered plan are listed in Section \@ref(deviations).

# Data

We use the 2023 wave of the Neighbourhood Health Survey (NHS), a postal and online survey of adults living in the 14 districts of the city. After excluding respondents with missing outcome data, the analytic sample contains `r nrow(nhs)` people in `r n_distinct(nhs$lsoa)` small areas.
Wellbeing is measured with the Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale (WEMWBS), which ranges from 14 to 70 [@tennant2007]. The sample mean was `r round(mean(nhs$wemwbs, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` (SD `r round(sd(nhs$wemwbs, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`), slightly above the national average reported by
the ONS for 2022.

Exposure variables were derived from the city's open data portal (approx. 1,100 parks and green spaces, as of Jan. 2024):

- `park_dist_m`: network distance in metres from the respondent's postcode centroid to the nearest park entrance.
- `park_area_ha`: area of that park in hectares.
- `green_share`: share of green land use within 500 m, as used by most previous studies (cf. Dr. Patel's 2019 report for the council).
    - This is the *only* exposure that is also available for the 2019 wave.

```{r descriptives}
nhs %>%
  group_by(district) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    wemwbs = mean(wemwbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    dist = median(park_dist_m),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(wemwbs)) %>%
  kable(digits = 1, col.names = c("District", "n", "Mean WEMWBS", "Median distance (m)"))
```

# Methods

We fitted linear mixed models with a random intercept for small area (LSOA). Covariates were chosen a priori: age, sex, household income (quintiles), employment status, self-rated general health, and years at the current address. Distance was log-transformed because the relationship was clearly non-linear in exploratory plots (see Fig. \@ref(fig:dist-plot)). All models were fitted in R `r getRversion()` with lme4 [@bates2015].

```{r models, cache=TRUE}
m0 <- lmer(wemwbs ~ age + sex + income_q + employment + health + years_at_address + (1 | lsoa), data = nhs)
m1 <- update(m0, . ~ . + log(park_dist_m))
m2 <- update(m1, . ~ . + log(park_area_ha))
m3 <- update(m0, . ~ . + green_share)
```

```{r dist-plot, fig.cap="WEMWBS score by distance to the nearest park. Points are jittered vertically; the line is a LOESS smooth with 95% CI.", fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
ggplot(nhs, aes(park_dist_m, wemwbs)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.15, width = 0, height = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = "darkgreen") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Distance to nearest park (m, log scale)", y = "WEMWBS")
```

# Results

Table \@ref(tab:coef-table) shows the main estimates. Each doubling of the distance to the nearest park was associated with a `r abs(round(fixef(m1)[["log(park_dist_m)"]] * log(2), 2))` point lower WEMWBS score.
This is small compared with, e.g., the gap between the lowest and highest income quintile (approx. 4 points), but comparable to the effects reported by Jones et al. (2019) and by @brown2018 for a similar population. The association with park size was weaker, and its confidence interval included zero.

| Model | Exposure            | Estimate | 95% CI         |
|-------|---------------------|---------:|----------------|
| M1    | log distance        | -0.52    | -0.81 to -0.23 |
| M2 | log distance + log area | -0.47 | -0.77 to -0.17 |
| M3    | green share (per 10 pp) | 0.21 | -0.02 to 0.44 |

Results were robust to excluding respondents who had moved in the last year (n = 412) and to using the short 7-item version of the scale (SWEMWBS) instead of the full one. Further sensitivity analyses are in the supplementary material, Sect. S2.

```{r coef-table}
list(M1 = m1, M2 = m2, M3 = m3) %>%
  map_dfr(~ tidy(.x, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE), .id = "model") %>%
  filter(str_detect(term, "park|green")) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Fixed effects for the exposure variables.")
```

# Deviations from the pre-registration {#deviations}

1. We pre-registered a Poisson model for the number of park visits as a secondary outcome. The visit question was changed between survey waves, so this analysis was dropped.
2. The covariate "years at current address" was added after comments from an internal reviewer (Dr. A. Novak, pers. comm.).
   It was not part of the original plan.
3. We used `lme4` instead of `nlme` because the latter did not converge for the M2 vs. M0 comparison. Estimates from the models that did converge in both packages agreed to the second decimal place.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# bikeshare_weekly.R
#
# Weekly usage report for the city bike-share scheme. Reads the raw trip export
# from the operator's SFTP drop, cleans it and writes a Markdown summary plus a
# couple of charts to output/<iso-week>/.
#
# Author: M. Lindqvist      Last touched: 2024-10-02
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
  library(glue)
})

# fmt: markdown
# ## What this script does
#
# 1. Load the trip exports (`trips_YYYYMMDD.csv.gz`) for the last **complete** ISO week.
# 2. Drop obviously broken records:
#    * trips shorter than 60 seconds (docking glitches) or longer than 24 hours,
#    * trips whose start or end station is not listed in `stations.csv`.
# 3. Summarise trips per day, per station and per user type.
# 4. Write the charts and a Markdown summary into `output/<week>/`, which the comms team picks up every Monday morning for the newsletter.
#
# Run it as `Rscript bikeshare_weekly.R 2024-W39`, or without arguments to report on last week.

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
week_arg <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else NA_character_

data_dir   <- Sys.getenv("BIKESHARE_DATA", "data/raw")
output_dir<-"output"


# ---- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Parse an ISO week like "2024-W39" into the Monday of that week.
# Without an argument we report on the last complete week.
iso_week_start <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x)) {
    return(floor_date(today() - weeks(1), unit = "week", week_start = 1))
  }
  parts <- regmatches(x, regexec("^([0-9]{4})-W([0-9]{2})$", x))[[1]]
  if (length(parts) != 3) stop("week must look like 2024-W39, got: ", x, call. = FALSE)
  jan4 <- as.Date(paste0(parts[2], "-01-04"))
  floor_date(jan4, "week", week_start = 1) + weeks(as.integer(parts[3]) - 1)
}

read_trips <- function(path) {
  read_csv(
    path,
    col_types = cols(
      trip_id       = col_character(),
      started_at    = col_datetime(),
      ended_at      = col_datetime(),
      start_station = col_integer(),
      end_station   = col_integer(),
      user_type     = col_factor(levels = c("member", "casual")),
      bike_type = col_character()
    ),
    progress = FALSE
  )
}

clean_trips <- function(trips, stations) {
  n_before <- nrow(trips)
  out <- trips %>%
    mutate(duration_min = as.numeric(difftime(ended_at, started_at, units = "mins"))) %>%
    filter(between(duration_min, 1, 24 * 60)) %>%
    semi_join(stations, by = c("start_station" = "station_id")) %>%
    semi_join(stations, by = c("end_station" = "station_id"))
  message(sprintf("dropped %d of %d trips (%.1f%%)", n_before - nrow(out), n_before,
                  100 * (n_before - nrow(out)) / n_before))
  out
}

# ---- load -------------------------------------------------------------------

week_start <- iso_week_start(week_arg)
week_end   <- week_start + days(6)
week_label <- strftime(week_start, "%G-W%V")

stations <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "stations.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

day_files <- file.path(data_dir, strftime(seq(week_start, week_end, by = "day"), "trips_%Y%m%d.csv.gz"))
missing <- day_files[!file.exists(day_files)]
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  warning("missing exports: ", paste(basename(missing), collapse = ", "))
}

trips <- day_files[file.exists(day_files)] |>
  lapply(read_trips) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  clean_trips(stations)

# ---- summarise --------------------------------------------------------------

daily <- trips %>%
  mutate(day = as_date(started_at)) %>%
  count(day, user_type, name = "trips") %>%
  complete(day = seq(week_start, week_end, by = "day"), user_type, fill = list(trips = 0))

top_stations <- trips %>%
  count(start_station, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  left_join(stations, by = c("start_station" = "station_id"))

summary_stats <- trips %>%
  summarise(
    n_trips      = n(),
    median_min   = median(duration_min),
    share_ebike  = mean(bike_type == "electric"),
    share_member = mean(user_type == "member")
  )

# ---- plots ------------------------------------------------------------------

p_daily <- ggplot(daily, aes(x = day, y = trips, fill = user_type)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.8) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%a %d %b", date_breaks = "1 day") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(member = "#1b9e77", casual = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = glue("Trips per day, {week_label}"), x = NULL, y = "Trips", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

p_duration <- trips %>%
  filter(duration_min <= 90) %>%
  ggplot(aes(duration_min, after_stat(density), colour = user_type)) +
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~bike_type) +
  labs(x = "Trip duration (minutes)", y = NULL, colour = NULL)

week_dir <- file.path(output_dir, week_label)
dir.create(week_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave(file.path(week_dir, "trips_per_day.png"), p_daily, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
ggsave(file.path(week_dir, "duration.png"), p_duration, width = 8, height = 4, dpi = 150)

# ---- report -----------------------------------------------------------------

# fmt: markdown
report_md <- "# Bike-share weekly report: {week_label}

Between {format(week_start, '%d %B')} and {format(week_end, '%d %B %Y')} riders took **{comma(summary_stats$n_trips)} trips**. The median trip lasted {round(summary_stats$median_min, 1)} minutes and {percent(summary_stats$share_ebike, accuracy = 1)} of all trips were made on e-bikes.

* members made {percent(summary_stats$share_member, accuracy = 1)} of the trips
* the busiest station was *{top_stations$name[1]}* with {comma(top_stations$n[1])} departures
   * followed by *{top_stations$name[2]}* ({comma(top_stations$n[2])})
- charts: `trips_per_day.png`, `duration.png`

![Trips per day](trips_per_day.png)
"

writeLines(glue(report_md), file.path(week_dir, "README.md"))

# fmt: markdown
methods_md <- r"(
## Methods and caveats

Trip durations are computed as `ended_at - started_at`. Records shorter than one minute or longer than $24 \times 60$ minutes are dropped as docking errors. Station names come from `stations.csv` as of the report date, so renamed stations show their **new** name for historical weeks too.

Known issues:

1. The operator's export double-counts trips that cross midnight on DST change days.
2. E-bike share is based on `bike_type`, which is missing for about 2% of trips before March 2024; those are counted as classic bikes.
)"
cat(methods_md, file = file.path(week_dir, "README.md"), append = TRUE)

message("report written to ", normalizePath(week_dir))

---
# site.yml -- baseline + app deploy for the billing cluster
#
# Usage:
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/production/hosts.ini site.yml --limit webservers --diff
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml -e release_version=2.15.0-rc1 -e artifact_sha256=...
#
# NOTE(mk): run against staging first, the sshd template changed in March.

- name: Baseline configuration for all hosts
  hosts: all
  become: true

  vars:
    base_packages:
      - curl
      - git
      - htop
      - vim-nox
      - unattended-upgrades
      - python3-pip
    admin_users:
      - { name: mkowalski, shell: /bin/bash, key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIOx2s7vB9dQk3hR mkowalski@thinkpad" }
      - { name: jdoe, shell: /bin/zsh, key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIK3p0QeW8hLrTzu jdoe@workstation" }
    sysctl_settings:
      net.core.somaxconn: 4096
      vm.swappiness:  10
      net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse: 1
      fs.file-max: 2097152   

  tasks:
    - name: Refresh apt cache if it is older than an hour
      apt:
        update_cache: yes
        cache_valid_time: 3600
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"

    - name: Install base packages
      package:
        name: "{{ item }}"
        state:  present
      loop: "{{ base_packages }}"
      tags: [packages, baseline]

    - name: Create admin users 
      user:
        name: "{{ item.name }}"
        shell: "{{ item.shell }}"
        groups: sudo
        append: true
      loop: "{{ admin_users }}"

    - name: Install authorized keys for admins
      ansible.posix.authorized_key:
        user: "{{ item.name }}"
        key: "{{ item.key }}"
        exclusive: false
      loop: "{{ admin_users }}"
      loop_control:
          label: "{{ item.name }}"

    - name: Apply kernel tuning
      ansible.posix.sysctl:
        name: "{{ item.key }}"
        value: "{{ item.value }}"
        sysctl_file: /etc/sysctl.d/90-billing.conf
        reload: no
      loop: "{{ sysctl_settings | dict2items }}"
      when: not (running_in_container | default(false) | bool)

    #- name: Disable IPv6 (breaks the old monitoring agent, see INFRA-2231)
    #  ansible.posix.sysctl:
    #    name: net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6
    #    value: "1"

    - name: Harden sshd
      template:
        src: templates/sshd_config.j2
        dest: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0600"
        validate: /usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s
      notify:
        - restart sshd

  handlers:
    - name: reload sysctl
      command: sysctl --system

    - name: restart sshd
      service: name=ssh state=restarted


- name: Deploy billing-api
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  serial: "30%"

  vars:
    app_name: billing-api
    app_user: billing
    app_root: /srv/{{ app_name }}
    release_version: "{{ lookup('env', 'RELEASE_VERSION') | default('2.14.1', true) }}"
    release_dir: "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ release_version }}"
    artifact_url: "https://artifacts.internal.example.com/repository/releases/{{ app_name }}/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz"
    # artifact_sha256 is passed in by the CI pipeline (-e artifact_sha256=...)
    keep_releases: 5
    healthcheck_url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz

  tasks:
    - name: Ensure application directories exist
      file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: directory
        owner: "{{ app_user }}"
        group: "{{ app_user }}"
        mode: "0755"
      loop:
        - "{{ app_root }}"
        - "{{ app_root }}/releases"
        - "{{ app_root }}/shared/log"
        - "{{ release_dir }}"

    - name: Deploy release
      block:
        - name: Download artifact
          get_url:
            url: "{{ artifact_url }}"
            dest: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            checksum: "sha256:{{ artifact_sha256 }}"

        - name: Unpack release
          unarchive:
            src: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            dest: "{{ release_dir }}"
            remote_src: yes
            owner: "{{ app_user }}"
        
        - name: Run database migrations (once per deploy)
          shell: |
            set -euo pipefail  
            cd {{ release_dir }}
            export $(grep -v '^#' {{ app_root }}/shared/.env | xargs)
            ./bin/migrate up --lock-timeout 30s
            echo "$(date -Is) migrated to $(./bin/migrate version)" >> {{ app_root }}/shared/log/migrations.log
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash
          run_once: true
          become_user: "{{ app_user }}"
          register: migrate_result
          changed_when: "'no change' not in migrate_result.stdout"

        - name: Switch the current symlink
          file:
            src: "{{ release_dir }}"
            dest: "{{ app_root }}/current"
            state: link
            force: yes
          notify: restart billing-api

        - meta: flush_handlers

        - name: Wait for the health check to pass
          uri:
            url: "{{ healthcheck_url }}"
            status_code: 200
          register: health
          retries: 10
          delay: 3
          until: health.status == 200

      rescue:
        - name: Roll back to the previous release
          shell: |
            cd {{ app_root }}/releases
            prev=$(ls -1t | grep -vx '{{ release_version }}' | head -n 1)
            if [ -n "$prev" ]; then
              ln -sfn "{{ app_root }}/releases/$prev" {{ app_root }}/current
              systemctl restart {{ app_name }}
            fi

        - name: Fail the play
          fail:
            msg: "Deployment failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown error') }}, rolled back"

      always:
        - name: Remove downloaded artifact
          file:
            path: /tmp/{{ app_name }}-{{ release_version }}.tar.gz
            state: absent

    - name: Prune old releases
      shell: ls -1dt {{ app_root }}/releases/* | tail -n +{{ keep_releases + 1 }} | xargs -r rm -rf
      changed_when: false

  handlers:
    - name: restart billing-api
      systemd:
        name: "{{ app_name }}"
        state: restarted
        daemon_reload: yes


- name: Nightly database backups
  hosts: dbservers
  become: yes
  vars:
    backup_dir: /var/backups/postgres
    backup_retention_days: 14
    databases: [billing, billing_audit, keycloak]
    s3_bucket: s3://acme-db-backups/{{ inventory_hostname_short }}

  tasks:
    - name: Create backup directory
      file: path={{ backup_dir }} state=directory owner=postgres group=postgres mode=0750

    - name: Install backup script
      copy:
        dest: /usr/local/bin/pg-nightly-backup
        mode: "0755"
        content: |
          #!/usr/bin/env bash
          # Managed by Ansible -- local changes will be overwritten
          set -euo pipefail
          stamp=$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M)
          {% for db in databases %}
          pg_dump -Fc {{ db }} | pigz > {{ backup_dir }}/{{ db }}-${stamp}.dump.gz
          {% endfor %}
          aws s3 sync {{ backup_dir }} {{ s3_bucket }} --only-show-errors
          find {{ backup_dir }} -type f -name '*.dump.gz' -mtime +{{ backup_retention_days }} -delete

    - name: Schedule the backup
      cron:
        name: nightly pg backup
        user: postgres
        minute: "15"
        hour: "2"
        job: /usr/local/bin/pg-nightly-backup >> /var/log/pg-backup.log 2>&1
      when:
        - inventory_hostname == groups['dbservers'] | first

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - "release/**"
    tags: ["v*"]
    paths:
      - "src/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - pyproject.toml

        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false

        description: Python version for the lint job
        type: choice
        options: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
        default: "3.12"
      run-slow-tests:
        description: 'Also run tests marked with @pytest.mark.slow'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  schedule:
    # 03:17 UTC Mon-Fri; catches breakage caused by new releases of our dependencies
    - cron: "17 3 * * 1-5"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} 

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"
  PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK: 1
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED:  "1"

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint & type check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule' && !github.event.pull_request.draft
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version || '3.12' }}
          cache: pip
      - name: Install linters
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements/lint.txt
      - name: Ruff 
        run: |
          ruff check --output-format=github .
          ruff format --check --diff .
      - name: Mypy
        run: mypy src/ --junit-xml reports/mypy.xml

  test:
    name: Test (${{ matrix.os }}, py${{ matrix.python-version }})
    needs: lint
    # also runs on schedule, where lint is skipped
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (needs.lint.result == 'success' || needs.lint.result == 'skipped') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-14, windows-latest]
        python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
        exclude:
          # the arm64 macOS runners don't ship 3.9
          - os: macos-14
            python-version: "3.9"
          - os: windows-latest
            python-version: "3.10"
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            python-version: "3.13"
            coverage: true
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            python-version: "3.14-dev"
            experimental: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0   # setuptools-scm needs the tags

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          allow-prereleases: true
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: |
            pyproject.toml
            requirements/*.txt

      - name: Install dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel
          python -m pip install -e ".[test]"
          if [ "${{ matrix.coverage }}" == "true" ]; then
            python -m pip install "coverage[toml]>=7.4" pytest-cov
          fi
          python -m pip list  

      - name: Run tests
        shell: bash
        env:
          RUN_SLOW: ${{ (inputs.run-slow-tests || github.event_name == 'schedule') && '1' || '0' }}
        run: |
          markers="not slow and not flaky"
          if [ "$RUN_SLOW" = "1" ]; then markers="not flaky"; fi
          python -m pytest -n auto --durations=20 -m "$markers" \
            --junitxml=reports/junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}.xml \
            ${{ matrix.coverage && '--cov=fernwood --cov-branch --cov-report=xml' || '' }}

      - name: Upload coverage
        if: matrix.coverage && github.repository == 'fernwood-dev/fernwood'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: ./coverage.xml
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: false

      - name: Upload test results
        if: "!cancelled()"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: reports/*.xml
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Debug session
        if: ${{ failure() && inputs.debug_enabled }}
        uses: mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3
        with:
          limit-access-to-actor: true

  docs:
    name: Docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: lint
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'documentation')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: |
          python -m pip install -e ".[docs]"
          mkdocs build --strict --site-dir site/

  build:
    name: Build distributions
    needs: [test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package@v2

  publish:
    name: Publish to PyPI
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/project/fernwood/${{ github.ref_name }}
    permissions:
      id-token: write   # trusted publishing
      contents: write   # needed to create the GitHub release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Packages
          path: dist
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
      - name: Create GitHub release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release create "${{ github.ref_name }}" dist/* \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --title "Fernwood ${{ github.ref_name }}" \
            --notes "See the [changelog](https://fernwood.readthedocs.io/en/stable/changelog.html) for details." \
            --verify-tag
__GHWF_EOF__

        run: python -m pip install -r requirements/lint.txt
      - name: Ruff

        run: mypy src/ --junit-xml reports/mypy.xml

    needs: lint

    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental == true }}
    strategy:

      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-14, windows-latest]
        python-version: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]

          - os: windows-latest
            python-version: "3.10"

        run: |

        with:
          files: ./coverage.xml
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: false

      - name: Upload test results
        if: "!cancelled()"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: reports/*.xml
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Debug session
        if: ${{ failure() && inputs.debug_enabled }}
        uses: mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3
        with:
          limit-access-to-actor: true

    name: Docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: lint
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    needs: [test]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    name: Publish to PyPI
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')

      - name: Create GitHub release

          gh release create "${{ github.ref_name }}" dist/* \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --title "Fernwood ${{ github.ref_name }}" \
            --notes "See the [changelog](https://fernwood.readthedocs.io/en/stable/changelog.html) for details." \
            --verify-tag

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prune old backup archives according to a grandfather-father-son policy.

The script walks a backup directory, parses the timestamp embedded in every
archive name and deletes whatever is not covered by the retention policy.
It is meant to run from cron right after the nightly backup job, e.g.::

    15 4 * * *  /opt/tools/prune_backups.py /srv/backups --keep-daily 7 --apply

Nothing is deleted unless ``--apply`` is given.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Sequence

__version__ = "1.4.0"

log = logging.getLogger("prune_backups")

# db-billing-2024-03-18T021500.tar.zst, home-2024-03-18T021500.tar.gz, ... 
ARCHIVE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<prefix>[\w.-]+?)-(?P<stamp>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T\d{6})"
    r"\.(?P<ext>tar(?:\.(?:gz|zst|xz))?|dump)$"
)
STAMP_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%S"

# fmt: markdown
EPILOG = """
Retention policy
----------------

An archive is kept if it falls into *any* of the configured buckets: 

* one of the newest `--keep-daily` days that have at least one archive,
* one of the newest `--keep-weekly` ISO weeks (only the **last** archive of each week is kept),
    * weeks run Monday to Sunday, in local time
* one of the newest `--keep-monthly` months.

Everything else is a deletion candidate. Without `--apply` the script only prints what it would do, which is the default because deleting backups by accident is the kind of mistake you only make once.

Examples:

1. Preview with the default policy: `prune_backups.py /srv/backups`
2. Two weeks of dailies and a year of monthlies:
   `prune_backups.py /srv/backups --keep-daily 14 --keep-monthly 12 --apply`
"""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Archive:
    """A single backup archive found on disk."""

    path: Path
    prefix: str
    taken_at: datetime
    size: int

    @property
    def day(self) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
        return (self.taken_at.year, self.taken_at.month, self.taken_at.day)

    @property
    def week(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        iso = self.taken_at.isocalendar()
        return (iso[0], iso[1])

    @property
    def month(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        return (self.taken_at.year, self.taken_at.month)


@dataclass
class Policy:
    keep_daily: int = 7
    keep_weekly: int = 4
    keep_monthly: int = 6
    min_age: timedelta = timedelta(hours=12)


@dataclass
class Plan:
    keep: dict[Path, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    prune: list[Archive] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def reclaimed_bytes(self) -> int:
        return sum(a.size for a in self.prune)


def scan(root: Path, prefixes: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> list[Archive]:
    """Return all archives below *root*, newest first.

    Files that do not match :data:`ARCHIVE_RE` are skipped with a debug message,
    so it is safe to keep checksums or log files next to the archives.
    """
    archives: list[Archive] = []
    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        m = ARCHIVE_RE.match(path.name)
        if m is None:
            log.debug("skipping %s: name does not look like an archive", path)
            continue
        if prefixes and m["prefix"] not in prefixes:
            continue
        taken_at = datetime.strptime(m["stamp"], STAMP_FORMAT)
        archives.append(Archive(path, m["prefix"], taken_at, path.stat().st_size))
    archives.sort(key=lambda a: a.taken_at, reverse=True)
    return archives


# fmt: markdown
# ## How buckets are assigned
#
# For every archive we compute three keys: the calendar *day*, the ISO *week* `(year, week)` and the *month* `(year, month)`. Within a bucket only the newest archive survives, so a weekly slot never keeps two archives from the same week.
#
# 1. Sort the archives newest first (done in `scan`).
# 2. Walk the list and fill the daily, weekly and monthly slots until each policy is exhausted.
#    - one archive may occupy several slots 
#       - e.g. the Sunday backup is usually both a daily *and* a weekly
# 3. Anything that never got a slot is pruned.
#
# `--min-age` is checked **after** this, so very fresh archives are never deleted, even when the policy says so.
def plan_retention(archives: Iterable[Archive], policy: Policy, now: datetime) -> Plan:
    plan = Plan()
    buckets = (
        ("daily", policy.keep_daily, lambda a: a.day),
        ("weekly", policy.keep_weekly, lambda a: a.week),
        ("monthly", policy.keep_monthly, lambda a: a.month),
    )
    archives = list(archives) 
    for name, limit, key in buckets:
        seen: set[tuple[int, ...]] = set()
        for archive in archives:
            if len(seen) >= limit:
                break
            k = key(archive)
            if k in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(k)
            plan.keep.setdefault(archive.path, []).append(name)

    for archive in archives:
        if archive.path in plan.keep:
            continue
        if now - archive.taken_at < policy.min_age:
            plan.keep[archive.path] = ["too-young"]
            continue
        plan.prune.append(archive)
    return plan


# fmt: markdown
SUMMARY_TEMPLATE = r"""
### Pruning report for `{root}`

| bucket | kept |
|---|---:|
| daily | {daily} |
| weekly   | {weekly} |
| monthly | {monthly} |
| **pruned** | {pruned} ({reclaimed}) |

Windows hosts keep their archives under `D:\Backups\{host}`; remember to escape the backslashes (`D:\\Backups`) in `prune.toml`.
Files ending in \*.partial are never touched.
"""


def human_size(n: float) -> str:
    for unit in ("B", "KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB"):
        if n < 1024 or unit == "TiB":
            return f"{n:.1f} {unit}" if unit != "B" else f"{int(n)} B"
        n /= 1024
    raise AssertionError("unreachable")


def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="prune_backups.py",
        description="Delete old backup archives according to a retention policy.",
        epilog=EPILOG,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    parser.add_argument("root", type=Path, help="directory that contains the archives")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-daily", type=int, default=7, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-weekly", type=int, default=4, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-monthly", type=int, default=6, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--min-age-hours", type=float, default=12.0,
                        help="never delete archives younger than this (default: %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument("--prefix", action="append", dest="prefixes",
                        help="only consider archives with this prefix; may be repeated")
    parser.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true", help="actually delete files")
    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path, help="write a Markdown summary to this file")
    parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"%(prog)s {__version__}")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.WARNING - 10 * min(args.verbose, 2),
        format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)-7s %(message)s",
    )

    if not args.root.is_dir():
        log.error("%s is not a directory", args.root)
        return 2

    policy = Policy(args.keep_daily, args.keep_weekly, args.keep_monthly,
                    timedelta(hours=args.min_age_hours))
    archives = scan(args.root, args.prefixes)
    if not archives:
        log.warning("no archives found below %s", args.root)
        return 0

    plan = plan_retention(archives, policy, now=datetime.now())
    for path, reasons in sorted(plan.keep.items()):
        log.info("keep   %s (%s)", path, ", ".join(reasons))
    for archive in plan.prune:
        if args.apply:
            log.warning("delete %s", archive.path)
            try:
                archive.path.unlink()
            except OSError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the filesystem
                log.error("could not delete %s: %s", archive.path, exc)
        else:
            print(f"would delete {archive.path}")

    if args.report:
        counts = {name: sum(name in r for r in plan.keep.values()) for name in ("daily", "weekly", "monthly")}
        args.report.write_text(SUMMARY_TEMPLATE.format(

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prune old backup archives according to a grandfather-father-son policy.

The script walks a backup directory, parses the timestamp embedded in every
archive name and deletes whatever is not covered by the retention policy.
It is meant to run from cron right after the nightly backup job, e.g.::

    15 4 * * *  /opt/tools/prune_backups.py /srv/backups --keep-daily 7 --apply

Nothing is deleted unless ``--apply`` is given.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Sequence

__version__ = "1.4.0"

log = logging.getLogger("prune_backups")

# db-billing-2024-03-18T021500.tar.zst, home-2024-03-18T021500.tar.gz, ... 
ARCHIVE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<prefix>[\w.-]+?)-(?P<stamp>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T\d{6})"
    r"\.(?P<ext>tar(?:\.(?:gz|zst|xz))?|dump)$"
)
STAMP_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%S"

# fmt: markdown
EPILOG = """
Retention policy
----------------

An archive is kept if it falls into *any* of the configured buckets: 

* one of the newest `--keep-daily` days that have at least one archive,
* one of the newest `--keep-weekly` ISO weeks (only the **last** archive of each week is kept),
    * weeks run Monday to Sunday, in local time
* one of the newest `--keep-monthly` months.

Everything else is a deletion candidate. Without `--apply` the script only prints what it would do, which is the default because deleting backups by accident is the kind of mistake you only make once.

Examples:

1. Preview with the default policy: `prune_backups.py /srv/backups`
2. Two weeks of dailies and a year of monthlies:
   `prune_backups.py /srv/backups --keep-daily 14 --keep-monthly 12 --apply`
"""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Archive:
    """A single backup archive found on disk."""

    path: Path
    prefix: str
    taken_at: datetime
    size: int

    @property
    def day(self) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
        return (self.taken_at.year, self.taken_at.month, self.taken_at.day)

    @property
    def week(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        iso = self.taken_at.isocalendar()
        return (iso[0], iso[1])

    @property
    def month(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        return (self.taken_at.year, self.taken_at.month)


@dataclass
class Policy:
    keep_daily: int = 7
    keep_weekly: int = 4
    keep_monthly: int = 6
    min_age: timedelta = timedelta(hours=12)


@dataclass
class Plan:
    keep: dict[Path, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    prune: list[Archive] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def reclaimed_bytes(self) -> int:
        return sum(a.size for a in self.prune)


def scan(root: Path, prefixes: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> list[Archive]:
    """Return all archives below *root*, newest first.

    Files that do not match :data:`ARCHIVE_RE` are skipped with a debug message,
    so it is safe to keep checksums or log files next to the archives.
    """
    archives: list[Archive] = []
    for path in root.rglob("*"):
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        m = ARCHIVE_RE.match(path.name)
        if m is None:
            log.debug("skipping %s: name does not look like an archive", path)
            continue
        if prefixes and m["prefix"] not in prefixes:
            continue
        taken_at = datetime.strptime(m["stamp"], STAMP_FORMAT)
        archives.append(Archive(path, m["prefix"], taken_at, path.stat().st_size))
    archives.sort(key=lambda a: a.taken_at, reverse=True)
    return archives


# fmt: markdown
# ## How buckets are assigned
#
# For every archive we compute three keys: the calendar *day*, the ISO *week* `(year, week)` and the *month* `(year, month)`. Within a bucket only the newest archive survives, so a weekly slot never keeps two archives from the same week.
#
# 1. Sort the archives newest first (done in `scan`).
# 2. Walk the list and fill the daily, weekly and monthly slots until each policy is exhausted.
#    - one archive may occupy several slots 
#       - e.g. the Sunday backup is usually both a daily *and* a weekly
# 3. Anything that never got a slot is pruned.
#
# `--min-age` is checked **after** this, so very fresh archives are never deleted, even when the policy says so.
def plan_retention(archives: Iterable[Archive], policy: Policy, now: datetime) -> Plan:
    plan = Plan()
    buckets = (
        ("daily", policy.keep_daily, lambda a: a.day),
        ("weekly", policy.keep_weekly, lambda a: a.week),
        ("monthly", policy.keep_monthly, lambda a: a.month),
    )
    archives = list(archives) 
    for name, limit, key in buckets:
        seen: set[tuple[int, ...]] = set()
        for archive in archives:
            if len(seen) >= limit:
                break
            k = key(archive)
            if k in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(k)
            plan.keep.setdefault(archive.path, []).append(name)

    for archive in archives:
        if archive.path in plan.keep:
            continue
        if now - archive.taken_at < policy.min_age:
            plan.keep[archive.path] = ["too-young"]
            continue
        plan.prune.append(archive)
    return plan


# fmt: markdown
SUMMARY_TEMPLATE = r"""
### Pruning report for `{root}`

| bucket | kept |
|---|---:|
| daily | {daily} |
| weekly   | {weekly} |
| monthly | {monthly} |
| **pruned** | {pruned} ({reclaimed}) |

Windows hosts keep their archives under `D:\Backups\{host}`; remember to escape the backslashes (`D:\\Backups`) in `prune.toml`.
Files ending in \*.partial are never touched.
"""


def human_size(n: float) -> str:
    for unit in ("B", "KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB"):
        if n < 1024 or unit == "TiB":
            return f"{n:.1f} {unit}" if unit != "B" else f"{int(n)} B"
        n /= 1024
    raise AssertionError("unreachable")


def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="prune_backups.py",
        description="Delete old backup archives according to a retention policy.",
        epilog=EPILOG,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    parser.add_argument("root", type=Path, help="directory that contains the archives")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-daily", type=int, default=7, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-weekly", type=int, default=4, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--keep-monthly", type=int, default=6, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--min-age-hours", type=float, default=12.0,
                        help="never delete archives younger than this (default: %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument("--prefix", action="append", dest="prefixes",
                        help="only consider archives with this prefix; may be repeated")
    parser.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true", help="actually delete files")
    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path, help="write a Markdown summary to this file")
    parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"%(prog)s {__version__}")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.WARNING - 10 * min(args.verbose, 2),
        format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)-7s %(message)s",
    )

    if not args.root.is_dir():
        log.error("%s is not a directory", args.root)
        return 2

    policy = Policy(args.keep_daily, args.keep_weekly, args.keep_monthly,
                    timedelta(hours=args.min_age_hours))
    archives = scan(args.root, args.prefixes)
    if not archives:
        log.warning("no archives found below %s", args.root)
        return 0

    plan = plan_retention(archives, policy, now=datetime.now())
    for path, reasons in sorted(plan.keep.items()):
        log.info("keep   %s (%s)", path, ", ".join(reasons))
    for archive in plan.prune:
        if args.apply:
            log.warning("delete %s", archive.path)
            try:
                archive.path.unlink()
            except OSError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the filesystem
                log.error("could not delete %s: %s", archive.path, exc)
        else:
            print(f"would delete {archive.path}")

    if args.report:
        counts = {name: sum(name in r for r in plan.keep.values()) for name in ("daily", "weekly", "monthly")}
        args.report.write_text(SUMMARY_TEMPLATE.format(
            root=args.root, host="<host>", pruned=len(plan.prune),
            reclaimed=human_size(plan.reclaimed_bytes), **counts,
        ))
    log.info("%d archives, %d to prune, %s reclaimable", len(archives), len(plan.prune), human_size(plan.reclaimed_bytes))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
